paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when you've blown it, you don't hide and you don't hand God a polished excuse. You tell Him the truth. David says it plain: "For I know my transgressions, and my sin is always before me." (Psalm 51:3) And he doesn't blame Nathan or anybody else, because he says "Against You, You only, have I sinned." (Psalm 51:4)

Now look at what David asks for. He doesn't ask God to patch him up. He prays, "Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me." (Psalm 51:10) That's not me scraping the burnt edges off a cookie and hoping nobody notices, that's a fresh batch, and only God can bake it. And David asks to stay close, because he prays, "Cast me not away from Your presence; take not Your Holy Spirit from me." (Psalm 51:11)

Then comes the part that gets me every time. God doesn't want a big show, because David says, "The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, You will not despise." (Psalm 51:17) So bring Him the honest heart, baker, even the heavy one, and bring it as it is. When God makes it new, you get the joy back, and you get something to say to others who've gone wrong, just like David: "Then I will teach transgressors Your ways, and sinners will return to You." (Psalm 51:13)
